title: "In Class Activity - Population Subdivision - Key"
author: "Rodney Dyer"
format: dyerlab-html
---

## Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
library( tidyverse )
px <- 0.2
py <- 0.8
pz <- 0.9
mxy <- 0.1
mxz <- 0.2
myz <- 0.3
N <- 100

df <- data.frame( Generation = seq( 0, N ),
                  px = c( px, rep( NA, N ) ),
                  py = c( py, rep( NA, N ) ),
                  pz = c( pz, rep( NA, N ) ) )

for( i in 2:nrow( df ) ) {
  df$px[i] <- df$px[i - 1] * (1 - (mxy + mxz)) + df$py[i - 1] * mxy + df$pz[i - 1] * mxz
  df$py[i] <- df$py[i - 1] * (1 - (mxy + myz)) + df$px[i - 1] * mxy + df$pz[i - 1] * myz
  df$pz[i] <- df$pz[i - 1] * (1 - (mxz + myz)) + df$px[i - 1] * mxz + df$py[i - 1] * myz
}

pivot_longer( df, cols = c( px, py, pz ), names_to = "Population", values_to = "Frequency" ) |>
  ggplot( aes( Generation, Frequency, color = Population ) ) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal()
```

With the original rates the three populations converge on the average of their starting frequencies, `r round( mean( c( px, py, pz ) ), 3 )`, within about 7 generations (every population within 0.01 of it).

## Question 1

```{r}
myz <- 0

df1 <- data.frame( Generation = seq( 0, N ),
                   px = c( px, rep( NA, N ) ),
                   py = c( py, rep( NA, N ) ),
                   pz = c( pz, rep( NA, N ) ) )

for( i in 2:nrow( df1 ) ) {
  df1$px[i] <- df1$px[i - 1] * (1 - (mxy + mxz)) + df1$py[i - 1] * mxy + df1$pz[i - 1] * mxz
  df1$py[i] <- df1$py[i - 1] * (1 - (mxy + myz)) + df1$px[i - 1] * mxy + df1$pz[i - 1] * myz
  df1$pz[i] <- df1$pz[i - 1] * (1 - (mxz + myz)) + df1$px[i - 1] * mxz + df1$py[i - 1] * myz
}

pivot_longer( df1, cols = c( px, py, pz ), names_to = "Population", values_to = "Frequency" ) |>
  ggplot( aes( Generation, Frequency, color = Population ) ) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal()

tail( df1, 1 )
```

`y` and `z` no longer exchange migrants directly, but both are still connected through `x`, and migration is still symmetric.  So the system ends up at the same place, the average of the starting frequencies (`r round( mean( c( px, py, pz ) ), 3 )`), but it takes about twice as long to get there (about 13 generations): `y` and `z` only converge on each other by way of `x`, and `y` now receives far fewer immigrants in total.

## Question 2

```{r}
myz <- 0.3
mzw <- 0.05
pw <- 0.1
N <- 200

df2 <- data.frame( Generation = seq( 0, N ),
                   px = c( px, rep( NA, N ) ),
                   py = c( py, rep( NA, N ) ),
                   pz = c( pz, rep( NA, N ) ),
                   pw = c( pw, rep( NA, N ) ) )

for( i in 2:nrow( df2 ) ) {
  df2$px[i] <- df2$px[i - 1] * (1 - (mxy + mxz)) + df2$py[i - 1] * mxy + df2$pz[i - 1] * mxz
  df2$py[i] <- df2$py[i - 1] * (1 - (mxy + myz)) + df2$px[i - 1] * mxy + df2$pz[i - 1] * myz
  df2$pz[i] <- df2$pz[i - 1] * (1 - (mxz + myz)) + df2$px[i - 1] * mxz + df2$py[i - 1] * myz
  df2$pw[i] <- df2$pw[i - 1] * (1 - mzw) + df2$pz[i - 1] * mzw
}

pivot_longer( df2, cols = c( px, py, pz, pw ), names_to = "Population", values_to = "Frequency" ) |>
  ggplot( aes( Generation, Frequency, color = Population ) ) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal()

tail( df2, 1 )
```

`z` does not receive anything back from `w`, so only `pw` gets a new term, and the equations for `x`, `y`, and `z` are unchanged.  At $m_{z \rightarrow w} = 0.05$, `w` closes only 5% of its remaining gap each generation and needs about 80 generations to get within 0.01 of its equilibrium, ten times longer than `x`, `y`, and `z` need.  Running 200 generations shows it clearly settled.

## Question 3

`w` ends up at `r round( mean( c( px, py, pz ) ), 3 )`, the equilibrium of the `x`–`y`–`z` system, and not at the average of all four starting frequencies (`r round( mean( c( px, py, pz, pw ) ), 3 )`).  Gene flow into `w` is one-way, like an island receiving migrants from a mainland, so the populations it receives migrants from set its equilibrium.  Adding `w` changes nothing for `x`, `y`, or `z`: emigration from `z` does not change `z`'s allele frequencies, and no migrants go back from `w`.
